##### **Transcript**

Around 10 years ago, the Financial Improvement Survey said that the number one issue behind insurance complaints was communication. Not price, not cover, but communication. Now Fast forward on to 2024, the FCA's latest value measures, the Which Super complaint and the data, it still tells the same story. People still don't understand what they've bought, claims are being declined because something wasn't explained, and complaints still surfacing in the same places. So. Over the next few weeks, I'm unpacking the data, the dilemmas, and the fixes. We'll talk about the policies, the patterns, and the human impact behind every rejected claim. Because complaints aren't just noise, they're signals. Signals that are telling you that something's not connecting. The Dilemma series. It continues tomorrow with a full lineup of upcoming topics I'll be covering. Watch this space.

  If a regulator shouts in the forest… and no one is around to hear them… do they make a sound?   Forget about why a regulator might be alone in a forest. It’s a metaphor.   Every year, regulators release new guidance, updates and expectations.   These are meant to protect clients, guide advisors and strengthen our industry.   Regulators rarely publish “optional” guidance. It’s often a heads-up about what’s coming next. A shift in expectations and what they’re focusing on.   But too often, these go unnoticed or unread.   Do you notice them?   Do you read them?   Or do you rely on your MGA to keep you informed? Or your insurance carrier?   Have you ever said to yourself or to another advisor, “When did that guidance come out?” or “I didn’t know that rule changed”?   By the time a deficiency is found or a client complains, the message that was meant to prepare you has turned into one that penalizes you.   Regulatory awareness isn’t about memorizing everything regulators publish. You need to be like Wayne Gretzky and “skate to where the puck is going” (another metaphor).   Do 3 things:   ·         𝗦𝗸𝗶𝗺 regulator updates weekly. Even just 10-15 minutes. ·         𝗞𝗲𝗲𝗽 a digital file of key regulator publications. ·         𝗗𝗶𝘀𝗰𝘂𝘀𝘀 regulatory updates with other advisors and your MGA’s compliance officer.   Regulators aren’t background noise. Recognize what matters and stay compliant.

  FCA Publishes Complaints Data for First Half of 2025 The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has released its latest complaints data, covering the period from 1st January to 30th June 2025. The report, published on 23rd October 2025, provides a detailed overview of complaints received and resolved by regulated firms during the first half of the year. It highlights emerging consumer trends, common problem areas, and the FCA’s expectations for how firms should respond. According to the data, total complaints increased slightly compared to the previous six months, with a notable rise in issues relating to consumer credit, motor finance, and current accounts. Many of these complaints stem from poor communication, unclear product terms, or delays in handling customer queries. The FCA noted that while complaint volumes fluctuate across sectors, the speed and quality of resolution remain key indicators of a firm’s overall conduct culture. The regulator also reiterated that firms must treat complaints as a valuable source of feedback rather than a compliance burden. Root cause analysis and proactive remediation were identified as areas where many firms still need improvement. The FCA expects senior management to regularly oversee compliance handling metrics and ensure that insights are used to enhance fairness and transparency in customer interactions. Firms should demonstrate that senior management is reviewing patterns. ⚖️ Firms must address the systemic issues behind repeated complaints rather than rely on reactive case handling. 🎯 Effective complaint management is a practical demonstration of delivering good outcomes under the Consumer Duty framework. ❗ Firms should ensure that internal MI, reporting accuracy, and record retention align with FCA expectations and DISP requirements. This publication reinforces the FCA’s ongoing focus on consumer outcomes and accountability. Strong complaint handling is not just about resolving issues, but about building lasting trust between firms and their customers.   The FCA's RegData report, REP008, is the 'Notification of Disciplinary Action relating to conduct rules staff (other than SMF managers)' which authorised firms have to complete annually covering the period 1 September to 31 August. As part of it's "reducing the regulatory burden" initiative, the FCA decided that as most firms never report from one year to the next, it would allow them to 'ignore' the REP008 in 2025 unless they had data to report. This is a different stance to all other RegData returns that firms have to complete, where ignoring any of them results in a potential fine. So naturally a lot of firms are nervous about just leaving REP008 on their Reporting Schedule, and today, the FCA has confused matters by sending out reminders to firms for REP008. The FCA have confirmed that if you do not have Disciplinary Action in the reporting period to declare, you are not required to submit a Nil Return. The data item will be removed from your schedule for this reporting period once the due date has passed and no further action will be required from you. At ICS we've almost inevitably had calls from firms worried about leaving REP008 just 'hanging' there. If you are concerned and looking for confirmation of this please get in touch.
